h: לַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב, ב׳ Tu B'Av, 2

p: In the Mishnah at the end of Taanis (Taanis 26b):
"There were no days as festive for Yisrael
'Go forth and gaze, O daughters of Tziyon,' and so on,
'on the day of his wedding and on the day of the gladness of his heart'
'On the day of his wedding' — this is Matan Torah;
'and on the day of the gladness of his heart' —
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
may it be rebuilt speedily in our days."
וּפֵירֵשׁ הָרַב עוֹבַדְיָה מִבַּרְטְנוּרָא (תַּעֲנִית ד, ח)
that "Matan Torah" refers to Yom Kippur,
on which the second Luchos were given,
and "the building of the Beis HaMikdash"
refers to its having been dedicated on Yom Kippur.
But it is a great strain to say
that "the building of the Beis HaMikdash"
which was so only in the First Temple,
as is stated in the Tosfos Yom Tov (ibid.).
Moreover, what is the meaning of the wording
with which they concluded in the Mishnah,
"may it be rebuilt speedily in our days"?
Was not the dedication of the Mikdash
One would be forced to say
that it is only in order to conclude
on a good note of redemption and salvation.
why did the Mishnah not count
on which the essential Matan Torah took place?
And regarding the fifteenth of Av
no support at all is stated in Scripture.
from the plain sense of the Mishnah
is that "on the day of his wedding"
the time of the giving of the second Luchos,
as Rashi and the Bartenura explain;
but "on the day of the gladness of his heart —
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
may it be rebuilt speedily in our days"
refers to the fifteenth of Av,
for the building of the future
will take place on the fifteenth of Av.
was destroyed in the sign of the lion — this is Av —
so too with the Beis HaMikdash of the time to come:
and will build the Beis HaMikdash
in the sign of the lion — this is Av.
is the day of the fifteenth of Av.
וּמַה שֶּׁלֹּא חָשְׁבוּ אֶת חַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת
As for why they did not count Shavuos
though it was "the day of His wedding,"
on which the Torah was given —
it is because with the first Luchos,
which came only from an awakening from Above,
there was as yet no assurance
וְלָזֶה לֹא נִקְרָא עוֹד יוֹם חֲתוּנָּתוֹ.
and therefore it was not yet called "the day of His wedding."
רַק דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי הַלּוּחוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת
Only specifically through the second Luchos,
which came from an awakening from below —
וְהוּא עִנְיַן הִתְרַבּוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and this is the increase of Torah she'b'al peh
from the side of the recipient,
כְּמַאֲמַר חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נְדָרִים כב, ב):
they would have been given only
the five books of the Torah
and the book of Yehoshua alone,
כִּי בְּרוֹב חׇכְמָה רָב כָּעַס (קֹהֶלֶת א, יח).
'For in much wisdom is much anger'" (Koheles 1:18).
הַיְינוּ שֶׁדַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי רוֹב כַּעַס
That is, specifically through much anger
the "much wisdom" became necessary to repair it,
which is the increase of Torah she'b'al peh
and the decrees of the Sages,
which the Sages make on their own,
and which is also called Torah
Therefore it is chiefly this that is fitting
to be called "the day of His wedding,"
for this is the essence of the marriage bond,
as the wording is written in the marriage document:
"And they shall have control over their property equally" —
meaning that the recipient will have the power
to make the Torah she'b'al peh,
from the side of the Giver.
This was completed specifically on Yom Kippur,
on which the second Luchos were given,
and this is called "the day of His wedding,"
the aspect of erusin, as mentioned above.
And "on the day of the gladness of His heart —
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
may it be rebuilt speedily in our days,"
for this will be the ultimate completeness of the union
in the Kodesh HaKodashim, through the Keruvim
שֶׁפְּנֵיהֶם אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו (שְׁמוֹת כה, כ),
whose faces are "each toward his brother" (Shemos 25:20);
וְנִקְרָא חֲדַר הַמִּטּוֹת (מְלָכִים ב יא, ב),
and it is called "the bedchamber" (Melachim II 11:2),
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא לְפִרְיָין וְרִבְיָין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל:
because it is for the fruitfulness and increase of Yisrael.
